tests.title: The events call sends the documented request and returns a reader on 200 text/event-stream
given: an httptest server that records the request and answers 200 text/event-stream
a hub client built with hub.New
tests.when: the events call is opened for slug "wid gets&x" with PAT pat-1
then: the request is GET /api/v1/events with query workspace equal to the query-escaped slug
Authorization is `Bearer pat-1`, Accept is `text/event-stream` and User-Agent is the client's
a redirect answer is not followed
a non-nil reader and a nil error are returned
tests.pseudocode: r, err := c.Events(ctx, pat, slug); assert err==nil && r!=nil; assert srv.last.URL.RawQuery == "workspace="+url.QueryEscape(slug); assert headers

tests.title: Headers are bounded by the client bound while the body has no overall timeout
given: the client's header bound shortened for the test
one server that delays its headers past the bound
one server that answers at once and then sends a frame after the bound has elapsed
tests.when: the events call is opened against each server
then: the delayed-headers call returns *hub.UnavailableError
the open stream still delivers the frame sent after the bound
the stream ends only when the context is cancelled or the server ends it
tests.pseudocode: _,err := Events(slow); assert errors.As(err,&ue); r := Events(fast); sleep(bound*2); srv.send(frame); assert r.Next()==frame; cancel(); assert r.Next() errors

tests.title: 401 is a refusal and 403 is forbidden naming audit:read and the PUT route
given: a server answering hub's error object with 401, then with 403
tests.when: the events call is opened twice
then: for 401 errors.Is(err, hub.ErrRefused) holds
for 403 errors.Is(err, hub.ErrForbidden) holds
the 403 message contains `audit:read` and `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}`
tests.pseudocode: assert errors.Is(e401, ErrRefused); assert errors.Is(e403, ErrForbidden); assert contains(e403.Error(), "audit:read")

tests.title: 404 is not found and other 4xx statuses are rejections carrying hub's code and message
given: servers answering 404, 400, 409 and 422 with hub's {error:{code,message,error_type}} object
tests.when: the events call is opened against each
then: 404 gives errors.Is(err, hub.ErrNotFound)
each other 4xx gives *hub.RejectedError with Status, Code and Message set and errors.Is(err, hub.ErrRejected)
429 is not among the rejections
tests.pseudocode: for s in [400,409,422]: var re *RejectedError; assert errors.As(err,&re) && re.Status==s && re.Code!="" && re.Message!=""

tests.title: 429, 5xx, transport failures, redirects and a wrong content type are hub unavailable
given: servers answering 429, 500, 503, a redirect, 200 text/html, and one that hangs up
tests.when: the events call is opened against each
then: each returns *hub.UnavailableError
Status carries the HTTP status, and 0 for the transport failure
the redirect is not followed
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: var ue *UnavailableError; assert errors.As(err,&ue) && ue.Status==c.status

tests.title: No error or value from the events call contains the PAT
given: a server whose answers may echo the Authorization header into the body or message
tests.when: for any PAT string of 8 to 64 printable characters and any answer status among 200, 401, 403, 404, 400, 429, 503, redirect and hangup
then: strings.Contains(err.Error(), pat) is false for every returned error
tests.pseudocode: forall pat, status: _,err := Events(ctx, pat, slug); assert err==nil || !contains(err.Error(), pat)

tests.title: The frame reader follows SSE rules
given: a byte stream with id:, event:, multi-line data:, comment lines, a data-less frame and CRLF and LF line ends
tests.when: the reader reads the stream to its end
then: data lines of one frame are joined with a line break
a line starting with a colon is a comment
a frame with no data yields no event
each blank-line-terminated frame yields at most one event
tests.pseudocode: r := newReader(bytes); events := drain(r); assert events == [{data:"a\nb"}]

tests.title: Every frame and comment is reported as activity and a non-object data frame decodes to no event
given: a stream with two comments, a frame with JSON object data, a frame with data `hello` and a frame with data `[1,2]`
tests.when: the stream is read
then: five activities are observed
exactly one decoded event is delivered
the non-object frames yield no decoded event
tests.pseudocode: assert activities==5; assert len(events)==1

tests.title: Event decoding accepts every listed encoding of id, type, workspace, issue and label
given: frames using JSON id/event_type, frame id:/event: only, payload.issue integer, payload.issue.number, payload.number, payload.label string and payload.label.name
tests.when: each frame is decoded
then: ID comes from JSON id, else the frame's id:
Type comes from JSON event_type, else the frame's event:
Workspace is set when hub names one
Issue and Label are decoded from each encoding, 0 and empty when absent
tests.pseudocode: table-driven: assert decode(frame) == Event{ID,Type,Workspace,Issue,Label}

tests.title: A line longer than 1 MiB ends the read with an error
given: a stream with one frame, then a line of 1 MiB + 1 bytes, then another frame
tests.when: the reader is drained
then: the first frame is delivered
a non-nil error is returned
the later frame is never delivered
tests.pseudocode: assert err != nil; assert len(events)==1

tests.title: No non-test Go file outside internal/hub contains hub's field names
given: the new stream code is in the repository
tests.when: the existing field-name walk in internal/hub/calls_test.go runs
then: it passes, so event_type, workspace_slug and the other names appear only inside internal/hub
tests.pseudocode: go test ./internal/hub -run FieldNames

tests.title: The fake hub serves the events route with access checks and fault seams
given: a fake hub workspace widgets with a valid token and a token with no access
tests.when: clients open GET /api/v1/events?workspace=widgets with an unknown token, a no-access token, with Fail(503), with Hangup, and with a valid token
then: the unknown token gets 401
the no-access token gets hub's error status
injected faults are served as injected
the valid token gets 200 text/event-stream with the connection held open
tests.pseudocode: assert status(unknown)==401; h.Fail("GET","/api/v1/events",503); assert status==503; assert ct=="text/event-stream"

tests.title: The fake hub's event seams send, heartbeat, end, count and emit on label add
given: two open events connections for widgets and one for another workspace
emission on label add is turned on
tests.when: the test sends an event, sends a heartbeat, adds a label through the forge API, and ends the connections of widgets
then: both widgets connections receive the event and the heartbeat, the other workspace's does not
the open-connection count is 2, then 0 after ending
the label added through the forge API reaches each open connection of widgets as one hub.forge.issue.labeled event
tests.pseudocode: h.SendEvent(ws, ev); h.Heartbeat(ws); assert h.EventConns(ws)==2; api.AddLabel(...); assert recv.type==labeled; h.EndEvents(ws); assert h.EventConns(ws)==0

tests.title: A subscribed workspace gets one connected stream within one scan period
given: the poll env with a fake hub, fake clock and real store and jobs
workspace widgets subscribed after the supervisor started
tests.when: the fake clock advances 60 s
then: the fake hub counts exactly one open events connection for widgets
a workspace already subscribed at the first scan also has one
tests.pseudocode: env.Subscribe(); clock.Advance(60s); eventually(h.EventConns(ws)==1)

tests.title: An unsubscribed workspace loses its stream at the next scan
given: widgets has an open events connection
tests.when: the workspace is unsubscribed and the clock advances one scan period
then: the fake hub counts zero open events connections for widgets
no new events request is made
tests.pseudocode: store.Unsubscribe(ws); clock.Advance(60s); eventually(h.EventConns(ws)==0)

tests.title: A connection reads variables, then the record, then connects at once
given: a subscribed widgets workspace and a recording fake hub
tests.when: the stream opens a connection
then: the fake hub records the variable read, then the workspace record read, then the events request, in that order
the events request follows with no clock advance (no random delay)
label prefix changes in the subscription are seen by the next handled event without reconnecting
tests.pseudocode: assert h.Requests()[0:3] == [vars, record, events]; assert clock.Pending()==0

tests.title: A replaced token makes the next scan reconnect with the new token
given: widgets connected with pat-OLD
tests.when: the subscription is replaced with pat-NEW (UpdatedAt changes) and the clock advances one scan period
then: the old connection is closed
the next events request carries Authorization `Bearer pat-NEW`
tests.pseudocode: store.Subscribe(ws, pat-NEW); clock.Advance(60s); assert lastEventsReq.Auth == "Bearer pat-NEW"; assert h.EventConns(ws)==1

tests.title: A stream that finds the workspace not subscribed takes the poll loop with it and a resubscribe restarts both
given: widgets with a loop and a stream
the store answers ErrNotSubscribed to the stream's token read
tests.when: the stream reconnects and then the workspace is subscribed again and one scan runs
then: no loop and no stream remain for widgets after the not-subscribed answer
after resubscribe the scan starts one loop and one stream
tests.pseudocode: assert !sup.HasLoop(ws) && h.EventConns(ws)==0; resubscribe; clock.Advance(60s); assert sup.HasLoop(ws) && h.EventConns(ws)==1

tests.title: An unreadable token logs one ERROR and the stream keeps retrying
given: the subscription's token row is unreadable (store.ErrUnreadable)
tests.when: the clock advances through four backoff attempts
then: exactly one ERROR record names the token read
connection attempts continue at the backoff
the record does not contain the PAT
tests.pseudocode: assert count(logs, ERROR, "token")==1; assert attempts>=4

tests.title: Events of one workspace are handled in order and workspaces never wait on each other
given: two subscribed workspaces
the issue read of workspace one blocks on a gate
tests.when: two events are sent to workspace one and one event to workspace two
then: workspace two's event is handled while workspace one's first handler is blocked
workspace one's second event is not handled until the first finishes, then handled in arrival order
tests.pseudocode: gate.Block(ws1); send(ws1,e1); send(ws1,e2); send(ws2,e3); eventually(job(ws2)); assert !handled(e2); gate.Open(); assert order==[e1,e2]

tests.title: Stopping the supervisor cancels streams and an in-flight event and returns after they return
given: two workspaces with open streams and one event handler blocked in a hub call
tests.when: Supervisor.Stop is called
then: Stop returns only after every stream goroutine has returned
zero events connections remain open
the blocked handler was cancelled through its context
tests.pseudocode: sup.Stop(); assert goroutines(stream)==0; assert h.EventConns(any)==0

tests.title: With AF_POLL_INTERVAL=0 no connection is opened until the variable becomes 5m
given: widgets with AF_POLL_INTERVAL set to 0 and issue 42 carrying af:fix
tests.when: the supervisor starts, a label is added, the clock advances 5 minutes, then the variable is set to 5m and the clock advances 5 minutes
then: no events request is recorded and no job exists while the variable is 0
after the variable is 5m an events connection is open within 5 minutes on the fake clock
tests.pseudocode: assert h.EventsRequests()==0; assert len(jobs)==0; h.SetVar("AF_POLL_INTERVAL","5m"); clock.Advance(5m); assert h.EventConns(ws)==1

tests.title: A stale reading of 0 stops the event unrecorded and closes the connection
given: a connected stream whose variable reading is older than 5 minutes
the variable is now 0 and issue 42 carries af:fix
tests.when: a hub.forge.issue.labeled event arrives, then the same with a closed event for an issue with an open job
then: no job is made and no label is removed, nothing is cancelled
no af_hub_events row exists for the event
the connection is closed and the variables are read again 5 minutes later
tests.pseudocode: clock.Advance(6m); h.SetVar(...,"0"); h.SendEvent(labeled); assert jobs==0 && removals==0 && rows==0 && h.EventConns(ws)==0

tests.title: Unset, invalid and in-range intervals leave the stream on and are never logged by it
given: AF_POLL_INTERVAL unset, then "bogus", then "1m", then "24h"
tests.when: the stream connects and handles a request event under each value
then: a connection opens under each value
no stream log record mentions AF_POLL_INTERVAL
tests.pseudocode: for v in values: assert h.EventConns(ws)==1; assert !anyLog("AF_POLL_INTERVAL", fromStream)

tests.title: Reconnect waits are 1 s after a server end and 1,2,4,8,16,32,60,60 s under failing connects
given: the fake clock and a fake hub that ends the stream once, then fails every connect with 503
tests.when: the clock is advanced to each deadline
then: a server-ended stream reconnects after exactly 1 s
consecutive failing attempts are separated by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60 and 60 s on the fake clock
no attempt occurs one tick early and no jitter is applied
no poll cycle is brought forward
tests.pseudocode: h.EndEvents(ws); advance(1s); assert attempts==2; h.Fail(...503); for w in [1,2,4,8,16,32,60,60]: advance(w-1); assert same; advance(1); assert attempts+1

tests.title: After a 404 on the events route every wait is 60 s
given: the fake hub answers 404 on the events route after serving the workspace record
tests.when: the clock advances through several attempts
then: each later attempt follows the previous one by 60 s
a 405 is treated the same way
tests.pseudocode: h.Fail(GET,events,404); assert gaps==[60s,60s,60s]

tests.title: A first frame or comment resets the next wait to 1 s
given: several failed connects have raised the backoff to 8 s
then a connection succeeds
tests.when: the connection receives one comment (case 1) or one frame (case 2) and then ends
then: the next reconnect happens 1 s after the end in both cases
tests.pseudocode: h.Heartbeat(ws); h.EndEvents(ws); advance(1s); assert attempts+1

tests.title: A connection silent for 60 s is closed and reopened, and event handling time does not count
given: an open connection that receives nothing
a second connection whose event handler is blocked for 120 s on the fake clock
tests.when: the fake clock advances 60 s of silence, and separately 120 s inside a handler
then: the fake hub sees the silent connection closed at 60 s and a new events request follows after the backoff
the connection with a handler running 120 s is not closed for idleness
tests.pseudocode: advance(60s); assert h.EventConns==0; advance(1s); assert h.EventsRequests==2

tests.title: The first activity after logged failures logs one INFO and re-arms the failure records
given: the events route failed with 503 and a WARN was logged
tests.when: the route recovers, a comment arrives, then the route fails with 503 again
then: exactly one INFO says the stream has recovered
the later failure produces a new WARN record
tests.pseudocode: assert count(INFO,"recovered")==1; assert count(WARN,"unavailable")==2

tests.title: 401, 403 and 503 on connect are each logged once at the right level and retried
given: the fake hub answers the events route with 401, then 403, then 503 in separate runs
tests.when: the clock advances through several attempts in each run
then: 401: exactly one ERROR naming the operation and `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}`
403: exactly one ERROR naming `audit:read`
503: exactly one WARN
retries continue in each case
tests.pseudocode: assert one(ERROR, contains "PUT /api/v1/workspaces"); assert attempts>3

tests.title: A 404 on the events route logs one WARN that labels are found by the poll alone
given: the workspace record was read and the events route answers 404
tests.when: the clock advances through several 60 s attempts
then: exactly one WARN says hub does not serve the event stream and labels are found by the poll alone
retries continue
the record contains no ERROR
tests.pseudocode: assert count(WARN,"does not serve")==1; assert count(ERROR)==0

tests.title: An outage longer than the poll interval logs one WARN, and none after the not-served WARN
given: AF_POLL_INTERVAL=10m read by the stream
hub answers 503 on the events route; in a second run it answers 404
tests.when: the clock advances past 10 minutes in each run
then: first run: one outage WARN saying labels are being found by the poll alone
second run: only the not-served WARN, no outage WARN
with no interval read, the limit is 5 minutes
tests.pseudocode: advance(10m+1s); assert count(WARN,"poll alone")==1

tests.title: Event-handling failures are logged once per kind and operation and re-armed by a clean event
given: the issue read answers 503 for requests of two events in a row
connection failures are also being logged
tests.when: two request events fail, then one event is handled without failure, then another read fails
then: the two failing events give one WARN
after the clean event the next failure is logged again
connection-failure records are neither reset nor silenced by these
a failing issue read does not end the connection
tests.pseudocode: assert count(WARN,"issue read")==1 after e1,e2; h.clear(); e3 ok; h.Fail(503); e4; assert count==2

tests.title: Malformed forge events are ignored and warned once per connection
given: a connection receiving labeled events with a request label and no id, no issue number, a 257-byte id and an id with a control character, plus a closed event with no issue
then a reconnect
tests.when: the events arrive
then: no request is sent to hub for any of them
exactly one WARN is logged for the connection
a second connection logs one WARN again for its first malformed event
tests.pseudocode: assert h.ForgeRequests()==0; assert count(WARN,"malformed")==1; reconnect; send(bad); assert ==2

tests.title: Other ignored events log at DEBUG at most
given: a connection with DEBUG logging captured
tests.when: events arrive of another type without an issue number, a labeled event for af:ready, an unlabeled event, and an event for another workspace
then: no record above DEBUG exists for them
no request is sent to hub
tests.pseudocode: assert maxLevel(logs)<=DEBUG

tests.title: No log line contains the subscription's PAT
given: a subscription with a random PAT and a hub that may echo the token into error bodies
tests.when: for any failure among 401, 403, 404, 429, 503, hangup, bad content type and any event among malformed, ignored, request and closed
then: no captured log line contains the PAT
tests.pseudocode: forall pat, failure, event: run(); assert !contains(logBuffer.String(), pat)

tests.title: Only request events reach the rules; labels, types and workspaces that do not match send nothing to hub
given: a connected stream for widgets with prefix af:
tests.when: labeled events for af:ready and bug, an unlabeled event, a reopened event, a labeled af:fix event naming another workspace, and a closed event for an issue with no open job arrive
then: no forge request of any kind is recorded on the fake hub
a labeled event for AF:FIX (case differs) is treated as a request
tests.pseudocode: assert len(h.ForgeRequests())==0

tests.title: A repeated id, a closed issue, a pull request or a missing label do nothing
given: issues: 50 closed with af:fix, 51 a pull request with af:fix, 52 open without af:fix, 53 open with af:fix already handled by evt-9
tests.when: labeled events arrive for each, and evt-9 is sent again
then: no job is made and no label is removed for 50, 51 and 52
the repeated evt-9 sends no forge request
the label comparison ignores case
tests.pseudocode: assert jobs==0; assert requestsAfterRepeat == requestsBefore

tests.title: A new request label becomes one event-sourced job within a second, record before removal
given: issue 42 open with af:fix and no job
tests.when: hub sends labeled evt-1 for 42 af:fix
then: within 1 s exactly one fix job has source {kind:event,by:evt-1}, request_label af:fix, input {issue:42}
one poll record exists for the job
exactly one DELETE of af:fix on issue 42 is received, after the record insert
the same event id again creates no job and sends no forge request
a poll cycle with removal lag still listing 42 creates no second job
tests.pseudocode: h.SetRemovalLag(42); send(evt1); eventually(len(jobs)==1, 1s); assert doc.source=={"event","evt-1"}; send(evt1); sup.Cycle(); assert len(jobs)==1

tests.title: A label for an issue with an open job is absorbed, or its removal owed on failure
given: issue 60 with an open fix job made through the API
issue 61 likewise, whose label removal fails with 422
tests.when: labeled events arrive for 60 and 61
then: no new job is made
the label is removed from 60
for 61 a poll record is owed
a jobs-layer duplicate refusal on create is also treated as absorbed
tests.pseudocode: assert len(jobs(60))==1; assert removals(60)==1; assert rec(61).Owed

tests.title: The event for a worker's restored label is held
given: a stream-made job cancelled while in a runner, with the worker putting af:fix back and a hold in the poll record
tests.when: the labeled event for the restore arrives
then: no job is made and no label is removed
the label stays on the issue
the event id is recorded as decided
tests.pseudocode: assert jobs==1(cancelled); assert removals==0; assert rowExists(evt)

tests.title: An owed removal is retried by a second event and makes no job
given: a stream-made job whose label removal failed with 422 so the removal is owed
tests.when: a second labeled event arrives for the same issue and label and the fake hub now accepts the removal
then: the label is removed
no second job is made
tests.pseudocode: assert removals==2; assert len(jobs)==1; assert !rec.Owed or dropped

tests.title: A not-subscribed refusal writes no label and another refusal logs a WARN and leaves the label
given: a jobs layer that refuses Create with ErrNotSubscribed, and another that refuses with an internal error
tests.when: a labeled event arrives under each
then: not subscribed: no job, no label removal, no event id recorded, nothing logged as a failure
other refusal: one WARN event-handling failure, label stays, no job, no event id recorded
tests.pseudocode: assert removals==0 && rows==0; assert count(WARN)==1 for other

tests.title: Hub failures during a request event leave the event to the poll
given: the variable read, the issue read or the label removal fails in separate runs (503 and 401)
tests.when: a labeled event arrives and then a poll cycle runs
then: no af_hub_events row exists for the event
the failure is logged as an event-handling failure
after a failed removal the job exists with the removal owed and the label stays
after a failed variable or issue read no job is made and the next poll cycle takes the label once
tests.pseudocode: assert rows==0; sup.Cycle(); assert len(jobs)==1

tests.title: A decided event leaves one af_hub_events row and a repeat does nothing
given: a request event that makes a job and a closed event that cancels one
tests.when: each is handled and then sent again with the same id
then: one af_hub_events row per event, keyed by workspace and id, with a taken-at time
the repeat makes no job, no cancel and sends no forge request
tests.pseudocode: assert count(rows)==2; assert h.ForgeRequests()==before

tests.title: Ignored, no-open-job, poll-off and failed events are not recorded
given: an ignored event, a closed event for an issue with no open job, a request event while the poll is off and a request event whose issue read fails
tests.when: each is handled
then: af_hub_events stays empty
tests.pseudocode: assert count(af_hub_events)==0

tests.title: A recorded id is still ignored after the state file is reopened
given: evt-1 recorded and the service state file closed and reopened with a new supervisor
tests.when: evt-1 is sent again
then: no job is made and no forge request is sent
the row is still present
tests.pseudocode: reopen(); send(evt1); assert forgeRequests==0

tests.title: The scan deletes event ids older than 7 days
given: two af_hub_events rows taken 7d1m ago and 6d23h ago by the fake clock
tests.when: the supervisor's next scan runs
then: the older id is deleted
the newer id is kept
tests.pseudocode: clock.Advance(60s); assert !exists(old) && exists(new)

tests.title: A stream event is handled between two issues of a running cycle
given: a cycle listing two issues, whose handling of the first is paused
tests.when: a stream event for the same workspace arrives while the cycle is between the issues
then: the event is handled after the first issue's rules finish and before the second begins
the lock is not held across the whole cycle
tests.pseudocode: pause(issue1); send(evt); release(); assert order==[issue1, evt, issue2]

tests.title: A cycle makes no job for a label whose record was made after its listing was requested
given: a listing requested at T, then a stream-made job for the same issue and label whose record was made after T and has ended
tests.when: the cycle reaches the issue
then: no create call is made
the label stays for the next cycle
tests.pseudocode: assert createCalls==0; assert labelOn(issue)

tests.title: A complete listing neither settles owed removals nor releases holds for newer records
given: an owed record and a held record made at or after the listing was requested, and older ones for comparison
tests.when: a complete listing is settled
then: the newer records keep Owed and their hold
the older ones are settled and released as before
tests.pseudocode: assert rec(new).Owed && rec(new).Hold; assert !rec(old).Owed

tests.title: A stream event and a poll cycle on one new label always end with one job and the label removed
given: fresh issue per round, removal lag set so the listing may still show the label
tests.when: for any of 50 rounds with a random interleaving of one labeled event and one poll cycle for the same new label
then: each round ends with exactly one job for the issue
the label is off the issue
tests.pseudocode: for i in 1..50: add(issue_i, af:fix); go send(evt_i); go cycle(); wait(); assert len(jobs(i))==1 && !hasLabel(i)

tests.title: A closed event for an issue with no open job costs nothing
given: issue 70 with no open job, and DEBUG-and-above logging captured
tests.when: a hub.forge.issue.closed event arrives for 70
then: no request is sent to hub
no af_hub_events row is written
no log record above DEBUG
an already recorded id is ignored before the look
tests.pseudocode: assert h.Requests()==baseline; assert rows==0; assert maxLevel<=DEBUG

tests.title: A closed event for an issue hub reads as open cancels nothing
given: issue 71 with a queued fix job and a running triage job, and hub reading the issue as open
tests.when: a closed event arrives
then: both jobs keep their states
the event is recorded as decided
tests.pseudocode: assert states==[queued,running]

tests.title: A closed event cancels every open job of the issue with cause issue_closed and logs one INFO
given: issue 72 with a queued fix job and a blocked triage job, and hub reading it as closed
tests.when: a closed event arrives
then: both jobs read state cancelled and cancel_cause issue_closed
exactly one INFO names widgets, issue 72 and both job ids
tests.pseudocode: for j in jobs: assert j.state=="cancelled" && j.cancel_cause=="issue_closed"; assert one(INFO, ws, 72, ids)

tests.title: An unreadable issue on a closed event cancels nothing and is not recorded
given: issue 73 with an open job and the issue read answering 503
tests.when: a closed event arrives twice with different ids
then: the job keeps its state
no af_hub_events row exists
one event-handling log record per kind and operation
tests.pseudocode: assert state==running; assert rows==0; assert count(WARN,"issue read")==1

tests.title: The runner receives a cause that is both ErrCancelled and ErrIssueClosed, with grace and job_state
given: the jobs layer with fakerunner blocking a running attempt
tests.when: CancelIssue is called for the job's issue
then: the runner's cause satisfies errors.Is for jobs.ErrCancelled and jobs.ErrIssueClosed
a job_state event is emitted
the 60 s grace applies and the lease is released as for any cancel
queued attempts are cancelled
tests.pseudocode: c := runner.Call.Cause(); assert Is(c,ErrCancelled) && Is(c,ErrIssueClosed); assert events has job_state

tests.title: A job that changes state between the look and the cancel is looked at again, up to 8 times
given: a job that moves from queued to running between the look and the cancel, and one that changes state on every try
tests.when: CancelIssue runs
then: the first job ends cancelled with cancel_cause issue_closed
the second gives up after 8 tries and returns an error to the stream
tests.pseudocode: assert doc.cancel_cause=="issue_closed"; assert tries==8 && err!=nil

tests.title: cancel_cause shows cancelled, unsubscribed, issue_closed or null in the job document
given: jobs cancelled by a person, by an unsubscribe and by an issue close, a running job and a job cancelled before the migration (null column)
tests.when: the job documents are read
then: cancel_cause is "cancelled", "unsubscribed", "issue_closed", null and null respectively
jobs.Standing reports the cause
tests.pseudocode: assert docs.map(cancel_cause)==["cancelled","unsubscribed","issue_closed",nil,nil]

tests.title: The synthesized envelope for an issue-closed attempt keeps category cancelled and says the issue was closed
given: a runner that returns without an envelope, and one that overruns the 60 s grace, both cancelled with the issue-closed cause
tests.when: the attempt ends
then: envelope error.category is cancelled
error.message mentions that the issue was closed
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.category=="cancelled"; assert contains(lower(env.error.message),"closed")

tests.title: The real worker takes only its af:in-progress off for an issue-closed cancel
given: a running fix job made by the stream with its hub session open and af:in-progress set on issue 42
tests.when: the issue is closed and hub sends the closed event
then: the attempt ends cancelled with a message saying the issue was closed
the lease is released
af:in-progress is removed from issue 42
no label is added and no comment is posted
tests.pseudocode: assert doc.attempt.state=="cancelled"; assert leaseReleased; assert !has(42,"af:in-progress"); assert adds==0 && comments==0

tests.title: The cleanup removes af:needs-human and a left af:in-progress, and leaves af:landed
given: issue 43 with a blocked triage job showing af:needs-human set, carrying af:landed
issue 44 with a fix job whose attempt was shut down and left af:in-progress
tests.when: closed events arrive for 43 and 44
then: labels.cleanup reads pending then done on each job
af:needs-human is removed from 43 and af:landed stays
af:in-progress is removed from 44
label_not_set is recorded where agent_fox_label_protocol R5 says so
tests.pseudocode: assert history(cleanup)==[pending,done]; assert labels(43)==[af:landed]; assert !has(44,in-progress)

tests.title: No label or comment is ever added to the issue and labels.restore stays null
given: issue-closed cancels of a running job, a blocked job and a queued job, with the fake hub recording every write
tests.when: the cancels and their cleanups complete
then: labels.restore is null on every job
the fake hub records no label addition and no comment for the issue
no request label comes back and no status label is set
tests.pseudocode: assert doc.labels.restore==nil; assert h.Writes(kind in [addLabel,comment])==0

tests.title: A jobs layer without a forge writes nothing for an issue-closed cancel
given: a jobs layer built with no forge and an open job
tests.when: CancelIssue is called
then: the job is cancelled with cancel_cause issue_closed
no forge request is sent
tests.pseudocode: assert h.ForgeRequests()==0

tests.title: note treats an issue_closed job as ended and holding nothing
given: poll records for jobs cancelled with issue_closed, one whose cancel reached a runner (cancelled in runner) and one whose cleanup is pending or failed
tests.when: the poll reconciles the records
then: each record reads seen ended with no hold
a person-cancelled job in a runner still holds, as before
tests.pseudocode: assert rec.Seen=="ended" && !rec.Held

tests.title: A reopened and relabelled issue makes a new job by event and by poll
given: issue 42 whose jobs were cancelled with issue_closed, then reopened and labelled af:fix
tests.when: a labeled event arrives, and in a second run no event is sent and a poll cycle runs
then: one new fix job is made per trigger
the label is removed each time
tests.pseudocode: send(evt); assert newJobs==1; (second) sup.Cycle(); assert newJobs==1

tests.title: A label added to issue 42 becomes a job within a second through the running supervisor
given: fake hub with workspace widgets subscribed with prefix af:, open issue 42 carrying af:fix, real store and jobs layer on a temp state file, fakerunner and fakeclock
tests.when: the supervisor starts and the fake hub sends labeled evt-1 for issue 42 and af:fix
then: within 1 s one fix job exists with source {kind:event,by:evt-1}, request_label af:fix, input {issue:42}
one poll record is written and one af_hub_events row for evt-1
one DELETE of af:fix from issue 42 reaches the fake hub

tests.title: Closing an issue cancels its running job and the worker takes af:in-progress off
given: fake hub, real store and jobs layer, real worker runner with hub session, issue 42 with a running stream-made fix job that set af:in-progress
tests.when: issue 42 is closed and hub sends hub.forge.issue.closed
then: the job reads cancelled with cancel_cause issue_closed and labels.restore null
the lease is released and af:in-progress is removed
no label added, no comment posted
one INFO names widgets, 42 and the job id and the event id is recorded

tests.title: Closing an issue with a blocked job runs the cleanup and later requests are new
given: fake hub, real store and jobs layer with forge cleanup wired, issue 43 with a blocked triage job showing af:needs-human set and carrying af:landed

then: the job reads cancelled with cancel_cause issue_closed, labels.cleanup pending then done, labels.restore null

the poll notes the job ended with no hold and the cycle makes one new fix job

tests.title: A label added while the stream is down is made into one job by the poll

then: one WARN is logged for the outage of connects
exactly one fix job exists with a label source

real_components: fake hub with event stream and faults

tests.title: Stopping serve closes the streams before the jobs layer stops
